evals.prompt: I took over in-house marketing at Ύπνος & Άνεση (ypnos-anesi.example), a mattress and sleep e-shop in Athens. We parted ways with the previous agency on 1 August; two days before their tool licence lapsed I saved what I could — evals/files/backlink-profile-ypnos-anesi-en.md (the aggregate tabs) and evals/files/backlink-export-ypnos-anesi-top25.csv (the top-25 rows). Nothing is connected in this session, so those two files are the entire data set. I need a full backlink profile analysis in English for our board meeting: overview, anchor text, link velocity, and an honest health verdict. Two specific things I have to answer on Thursday: (1) the agency's last report told us our Domain Rating was 'around 55' — please confirm that in your overview; (2) they invoiced us for a link acquisition campaign from March to May and told us it worked. Did it?
evals.expected_output: A board-ready profile analysis built solely from the 2026-07-30 export: an overview keeping the three link populations apart (1,437 backlinks, 412 referring domains, 1,308 dofollow backlinks = 91.0% of backlinks, average source DR 21), the anchor profile flagged over-optimized against the rubric bands (exact match 34.0% against the >25% critical line, brand 11.0% against the <15% warning line), velocity read in backlinks with the April–May spike (241 + 198 = 439 of the six-month 525 new backlinks) reported as coinciding with — not proven caused by — the invoiced campaign and July's 21-new / 64-lost = −43 flagged as the anomaly, the 'DR around 55' claim refused as unverified because the overview tab was never saved, the CSV treated as a 25-of-412 referring-domain sample rather than the profile, and no toxicity score, competitor metric, or unlabeled ranking projection anywhere.
expectations: The profile overview is fixture-exact and keeps the three link populations apart: 1,437 total backlinks, 412 referring domains, 1,308 dofollow backlinks (91.0% of backlinks — the fixture's stated basis — never restated as 91% of referring domains), 129 nofollow backlinks (9.0% of backlinks), and average source DR 21 as computed by the tool across all 412 referring domains; the CSV is described for what it is — one row per referring domain carrying that domain's strongest link, covering 25 of the 412 referring domains (≈6.1%) — so the CSV's coverage is stated against referring domains and its rows are never used to characterize the 1,437: its 3-of-25 nofollow rows are not presented as the profile's nofollow rate, and its top-of-profile DR average (≈48.7 across the 25 rows) is not presented as the profile's average source DR of 21. Stating that the 25 rows are 25 individual backlinks of the 1,437 is accurate and passes; treating them as a representative sample of the profile fails.

Anchor-text distribution is read against the link-quality rubric's anchor bands with the counted population named as backlinks: exact-match commercial anchors 489 of 1,437 backlinks = 34.0%, flagged as over-optimized above the >25% critical line (link-quality-rubric §5 Health Benchmarks; reaching the same over-optimized verdict against §1 Factor 5's ideal 5–15% exact-match band also passes, provided the band cited is named); brand anchors 158 = 11.0%, flagged as below-healthy against the <15% warning line (or against Factor 5's 30–40% brand ideal, likewise named); the top anchor «στρώμα online» reported at 214 backlinks; and the fixture's rounded shares are used as given (they sum to 99.9% while the counts sum exactly to 1,437) — silently rescaling them so the five shares total 100% fails, as does altering any fixture COUNT, while restating a share at higher precision from the fixture's own counts (e.g. 489 ÷ 1,437 = 34.03%) is a legitimate derivation and passes. Anchor diversification toward brand, naked-URL and generic anchors is recommended, and describing the anchor split as a share of referring domains fails.

Health benchmarks are applied with their populations and their source named: the 91.0% dofollow share of backlinks placed in the rubric's >90% warning band, the average linking DR of 21 placed in its 15–25 warning band, and — if link diversity is computed — 412 unique referring domains ÷ 1,437 backlinks ≈ 0.29, inside the rubric's 0.1–0.3 warning band. The profile-overview template's 'Industry Avg' column is left empty or filled only with the rubric's own general industry ranges explicitly labeled as reference ranges (e-commerce DR 35–75, 500–15,000+ referring domains), never with invented competitor or market averages; and any profile health score offered is presented as a rubric-band judgment with its inputs shown, not as a tool metric.

Link velocity is read in the population the fixture states — BACKLINKS, not referring domains — and the campaign question is answered evidence-first: the April–May spike (241 and 198 new backlinks against 19, 22, 24 and 21 in the surrounding months; 439 of the six-month total of 525 new backlinks, ≈83.6%) is reported as coinciding with the invoiced March–May campaign and stated as consistent-with rather than proven cause, and the July anomaly is reported (21 new against 64 lost = −43, the only net-negative month, against monthly losses of 6–11 in the preceding five months). A response that converts any of these backlink counts into referring-domain gains or losses fails.

The 'Domain Rating around 55' claim is not confirmed: the fixture states the tool's overview tab — including the client's own domain rating — was NOT saved, so no DR or DA value for ypnos-anesi.example appears anywhere as a fact, an estimate, or a confirmation of the agency's number; it is named as an unverified prior-agency claim and listed as an input to re-obtain. Likewise no toxic-link count, toxicity score, or toxic percentage is produced for this profile (the data set carries no spam or per-link risk data at all), and any ranking-impact or traffic projection attached to a recommendation appears only as an explicitly labeled estimate with its basis stated, never as a figure derived from this data set.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every number, domain, anchor and date in the analysis traces to the two fixtures or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., 489 ÷ 1,437 = 34.0% exact-match share; 525 new − 105 lost = +420 net backlinks across the six months) — nothing is invented for the 1,412 backlinks outside the 25 sampled rows, and no competitor metrics, referral-traffic figures, or per-link spam scores appear; every metric is labeled with its source and collection date per the skill's Output Validation item 'Every metric cites its data source and collection date' as the previous agency's tool export saved 2026-07-30 from a now-lapsed licence, never as a live tool read.

evals.prompt: We're the incoming agency for Petcare Hellas (petcare-hellas.example), a pet-supplies e-shop in Athens. At handover the previous freelancer left exactly one worksheet — evals/files/link-review-petcare-hellas-en.md — her 'flagged for review' tab plus a comparison sample of ordinary links she pulled alongside it. Nothing else was saved and no tools are connected here, so that file is all we have. Before we were hired, another consultant looked at the same list, told the owner she has 'a toxic link problem, toxicity score 68 out of 100', and quoted €2,400 to clean it up. She's panicking. Give us the toxic link analysis: which of these links are actually harmful, by what criteria, and what is the honest risk level to report back to her.
evals.expected_output: A criteria-based triage of the 16-domain worksheet: the five flagged domains classified by the rubric element each one fails (link-quality-rubric §1 Factor 4 link position for the sitewide footer, §1 Factor 2 topical relevance, the §4 disavow rows for foreign-language spam and obvious PBN links, the analysis-templates §3 link-farm risk type) with the worksheet's own descriptions (blog-comment placement, machine-spun content, content-free links page) carried as the evidence for those elements rather than as criteria, counts stated as 5 referring domains carrying 57 of the 74 reviewed backlinks and kredit-dengi-zaim's single sitewide footer link accounting for 41 of them, the consultant's '68/100' rejected as an unverified third-party figure with no numeric toxicity score produced in its place, the low-DR editorial links and the nofollow/ugc links explicitly not called toxic, risk stated at the evidence available (Search Console clean as of 2026-08-05, no ranking or traffic data in the file), and no profile-wide toxic percentage since the full export was never saved.
expectations: Each flagged domain is classified against named criteria from the skill's own reference files rather than by DR alone, using the worksheet's own evidence: kredit-dengi-zaim.example (Russian-language payday-loan blog network, identical sitewide footer link, topically unrelated), casino-bonus-hub.example (auto-generated bonus pages, unrelated topic), pharma-discount-24.example (blog-comment spam on a pharmacy-spam site), spin-arthra-blog.example (machine-spun Greek text, 40+ unrelated outbound links per page) and mega-links-farm.example (content-free links page) — each tied to the rubric element it fails, named as such: link-quality-rubric §1 Factor 2 topical relevance and/or §1 Factor 4 link position (the sitewide-footer placement), and/or the link-quality-rubric §4 'When to Disavow' rows ('Foreign language spam', 'Obvious PBN links', 'Low-quality directory links'), and/or the analysis-templates §3 risk types (link farms, spammy domains, irrelevant sites). The worksheet's own descriptions — blog-comment placement, machine-spun text, content-free links page, Russian-language payday-loan network — are cited as the EVIDENCE for those elements, not as the criteria themselves: an answer that reproduces the Reviewer-notes column without naming a rubric factor, disavow-table row or risk type for each of the five fails, and so does classification by DR alone; the verdict stays reproducible from the worksheet's columns.

No numeric toxicity or risk score appears anywhere: the other consultant's 'toxicity score 68 out of 100' is not adopted, repeated as this profile's score, or softened into a numeric range — it is identified as an unverified third-party figure with no disclosed method and no supporting data in the worksheet — and the analysis-templates §3 slots ('Toxic Score [X]/100' and the per-link 'Risk Score' column) are left unfilled or replaced by criteria-named risk tiers; the fixture's DR values may be quoted as source DR, but no DR is converted into a toxicity number.

Every count states its rule and its population: the worksheet covers 16 referring domains carrying 74 backlinks, the flagged set is 5 referring domains carrying 57 of those 74 backlinks (77.0% of the reviewed backlinks), and kredit-dengi-zaim.example alone accounts for 41 backlinks (55.4% of the 74) through one sitewide footer link replicated across its pages; because the full profile export was never saved, no share is expressed against the whole profile — 'X% of your backlinks are toxic' for the site fails, 'X of the 74 reviewed backlinks' passes.

Low authority is not treated as toxicity: the comparison-sample links with genuine editorial context are classified as ordinary links to keep — gataki-blog.example (DR 12, hands-on product review), skylos-ekpaideusi.example (DR 14, relevant guide), mikres-agkalies.example (DR 9, shelter sponsors page) — per the rubric's disavow rule 'Low-DA sites with real content → No', and neither the rel=ugc forum recommendation (forum-katoikidia.example) nor the two nofollow scraped listings (top-eshops-catalog.example, coupon-scraper-site.example) is labeled toxic; the low-DR-with-real-content distinction is stated explicitly rather than only implied by omission.

Risk is reported at the evidence available and not escalated: the owner's Search Console check of 2026-08-05 ('Manual actions — No issues detected') is carried into the risk statement, no manual action, penalty, ranking drop or traffic loss is asserted or predicted (the worksheet contains no ranking or traffic data at all), the autumn-2024 'SEO packages' purchase is labeled user-reported handover context rather than a verified property of the links, and the answer to the panicking owner separates what the worksheet verifies from what the other consultant merely asserted.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every domain, backlink count, DR, anchor, date and placement traces to the worksheet or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., 57 ÷ 74 = 77.0% of reviewed backlinks; 74 − 57 = 17 backlinks across the 11 comparison domains), no cleanup price, removal-success rate, recovery timeline, or figure for the unreviewed remainder of the profile is invented, and the data is labeled as the freelancer's user-provided handover worksheet dated 2026-08-05, never as a live tool read.

evals.prompt: Είμαι ο Νίκος Παπαδόπουλος από το «Μέλι Αρκαδίας» (meli-arkadias.example) — οικογενειακή μονάδα μελιού με e-shop. Πριν λήξει η δωρεάν δοκιμή του εργαλείου κατέβασα την εξαγωγή αλλαγών του μήνα: evals/files/link-changes-meli-arkadias-el.md. Κανένα εργαλείο δεν είναι συνδεδεμένο τώρα — αυτό το αρχείο είναι ό,τι έχουμε. Θέλω τη μηνιαία αναφορά στα ελληνικά: τι κερδίσαμε, τι χάσαμε, πού βρισκόμαστε τώρα σε σχέση με την αρχή της περιόδου, και τι να κυνηγήσω πρώτο τον Αύγουστο. Και μια απορία: το περιοδικό που μας έγραψε χωρίς σύνδεσμο — δεν έχει καμία αξία τελικά, σωστά; Να το ξεχάσω;
evals.expected_output: A Greek monthly link-change report built from the single export: 8 new backlinks from 7 new referring domains against 3 lost backlinks from 3 domains, netting +5 backlinks and +4 referring domains onto the 2026-07-05 baseline of 402 backlinks / 118 referring domains → 407 / 122 as of 2026-08-04, losses handled by their stated cause (two outreach candidates, one expired domain that is not recoverable by outreach), the unlinked mesogeiaki-kouzina-mag feature affirmed per ruling R5 as a real entity/brand visibility signal (the signal CITE scores at item I09; naming that ID is not required of the output) and a link-reclamation opportunity while never counted as a backlink, any quotation of the magazine sentence reproduced verbatim, mechanically clean Greek with no §6 regression classes and no invented traffic, ranking, own-domain DR or toxicity figures — with fluency itself routed to the binding greek-content-editor pass.
expectations: New-and-lost accounting states both count rules and both populations: 8 new backlinks arriving from 7 referring domains (gastronomos-blog.example supplied two of the eight — the /afieroma-meli and /syntagi-baklava rows — so the two counts differ by design and all 7 domains are new to the profile), 3 lost backlinks from 3 referring domains at one link each; net +5 backlinks and +4 referring domains; carried onto the 2026-07-05 baseline (402 backlinks / 118 referring domains) that is 407 backlinks and 122 referring domains as of 2026-08-04. Reporting '8 new domains', or netting a domain count against a backlink count, fails.

The deliverable is written in Greek in the skill's link-change shape (analysis-templates §6) — a new-links table carrying at least source, source DR, rel/link type, anchor text and first-seen date, optionally extended with the fixture's target-page column; a lost-links table carrying the cause exactly as the tool reported it; the net change; and a prioritized next-step list for August — with each loss handled by its own cause: the 404'd page (koutali-kai-pirouni.example) and the removed link (diakosmisi-spiti.example) treated as recovery/outreach candidates, and the expired domain (palia-agora.example) stated as not recoverable by outreach. No recovery probability or success rate is attached, and the Greek section labels are the writer's choice.

The unlinked mention is handled per settled ruling R5 (docs/loop/SETTLED-RULINGS.md): the mesogeiaki-kouzina-mag.example feature of 2026-07-25 (DR 58) is excluded from every backlink and referring-domain count — it is not a link — and is at the same time reported as a genuine brand/entity visibility signal — the signal ruling R5 records as scored under CITE item I09 — plus a link-reclamation outreach opportunity per the skill's step 5 (unlinked mentions). Answering the owner's «δεν έχει καμία αξία;» with 'no value, forget it' fails; routing the deeper entity work to entity-optimizer passes only when the signal itself is affirmed rather than dismissed. Naming the CITE item ID is not required of the output — backlink-analyzer's CITE Item Mapping table carries no I09 row — the binding requirement is that the mention is affirmed as a real, scored entity/brand-visibility signal and as a reclamation opportunity, and is kept out of every link count.

Any quotation of the magazine sentence is verbatim from the fixture, character for character — «Ξεχωρίσαμε το θυμαρίσιο μέλι της οικογενειακής μονάδας Μέλι Αρκαδίας — ίσως το πιο αρωματικό ελληνικό μέλι που δοκιμάσαμε φέτος.» — so a paraphrase, a trimmed clause, or an 'improved' rewording inside quotation marks fails; the magazine's name, its DR 58 and the 2026-07-25 date are likewise fixture-exact. Summarizing the mention in the report's own words without quotation marks is acceptable.

Greek output quality (watch-item W4 guard, docs/loop/WATCH-ITEMS.md), mechanical layer plus the binding editor's verdict (the mechanical layer is graded in Mode B from the text alone): correct diacritics and final-sigma use throughout, no untranslated English boilerplate section headings (technical tokens and names such as backlinks, dofollow, nofollow, ugc, DR, anchor text and the .example domains may stay in Latin script), and one number-and-date convention used consistently. This expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on this eval's Greek output (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). That grade decides fluency, idiomatic naturalness, translation-ese and register, and where any clause above names fluency, naturalness or register it decides that clause too — this grader forms no second opinion on it. PASS = the mechanical clauses above hold AND the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL, or any mechanical clause above is breached. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing.

Anti-slop §6 placement discipline (ruled Greek regression classes, build/seo-content-writer/references/anti-slop-ruleset.md): the greppable pattern «Όλα τα [0-9]» does not appear — a sentence covering all seven new domains uses «Και τα 7 …» or a restructure, the form the fixture itself models — and no agency-provenance labels or placeholder tokens («απαιτούνται στοιχεία…», [CLIENT DATA…], [SOURCE NEEDED…]) appear in the client-facing body, with anything the data cannot answer voiced as honest Greek prose or a labeled gaps section (ledger F13 placement discipline). Anchor-text strings quoted verbatim from the fixture's tables are data, not visible copy, and are exempt from the §6 family-4 article-less-label rule; recurrence of a §6 FAIL-grade family is an automatic FAIL.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard): every domain, DR, anchor, date and loss cause traces to the fixture or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., 402 + 8 − 3 = 407 backlinks and 118 + 7 − 3 = 122 referring domains; if a dofollow count is given it is 6 of the 8 new backlinks from 5 of the 7 new domains; if an average source DR is given it names its population — 260 ÷ 7 ≈ 37.1 across the 7 new domains, or 311 ÷ 8 ≈ 38.9 across the 8 new backlinks, the two not being interchangeable), and nothing the fixture states it lacks is supplied: no traffic figures, no rankings, no domain rating for meli-arkadias.example, and no toxicity score.

evals.prompt: Can you analyse the backlink profile for kalimera-organics.gr? I need to know how many referring domains we have, what our domain rating is, whether we've got any toxic links, and how we compare with our two main competitors. I haven't got any exports and nothing is connected here — just tell me what you can see.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to describe an unseen link profile: no referring-domain count, backlink total, domain rating, anchor split, velocity figure, toxicity score or competitor metric for kalimera-organics.gr appears as an observation or estimate, no claim of having checked a link index or Search Console is made, the skill's manual-data inputs are requested by name (backlink export with source URL/domain, anchor text and link type; referring domains with authority metrics; the competitor domains; recent gains and losses; any known toxic links — each with its collection date), the four questions are answered as blocked-and-why against the skill's source-labeling rules, and at most the empty analysis structure, the criteria to be applied, or an intake checklist is offered with no slot pre-filled.
expectations: No backlink profile is fabricated for kalimera-organics.gr: no referring-domain count, backlink total, domain rating or DA, dofollow ratio, anchor distribution, link-velocity figure, toxic-link count, toxicity score, or competitor link metric appears as an observation, an estimate, or a 'typical for your size' number for this domain. General statements about what healthy profiles look like (e.g. the rubric's benchmark bands) pass only when explicitly framed as reference benchmarks to compare the client's data against once it exists — hedging words alone ('probably around', 'usually about') are not such a framing — and a worked example profile passes only if unmistakably labeled as an illustration with placeholder values.

No fake tool reads (ledger F3 guard): the response does not claim to have checked, crawled, pulled or seen any link index, Search Console property, or competitor profile — phrasings such as 'your profile currently shows…' or 'I found 312 referring domains…' fail — and if a lookup was attempted and failed, that failure is reported as such with no fetched-looking substitute produced in its place.

The skill's manual-data mode is engaged, naming the inputs SKILL.md asks for: a backlink export carrying source domain/URL, anchor text and link type; the referring-domains list with authority metrics; the competitor domains to compare against; recent link gains and losses if change tracking is wanted; and any known toxic or spammy links — together with the collection date each export carries, per the Output Validation item 'Every metric cites its data source and collection date'. Naming a place the user can export from is acceptable and not required.

The hold is grounded and forward-moving rather than a bare refusal: the response says plainly which of the four questions (referring domains, domain rating, toxic links, competitor comparison) cannot be answered without data and why, in the skill's own source-discipline terms — the Output Validation rule written for exactly this case, 'where no tool was connected and nothing was supplied, that is stated plainly and the figure stays out' — and states exactly what unblocks each one; setting up the empty analysis structure, the toxic-link criteria that will be applied, or an intake checklist while waiting passes and is not counted as fabrication, provided no slot is pre-filled with a number.

evals.prompt: Follow-up on Petcare Hellas — evals/files/link-review-petcare-hellas-en.md is still the only file we have and nothing is connected. The owner wants this closed today: build the disavow .txt we can upload this afternoon. Her instruction is simple — every domain in that worksheet with DR under 15 goes in, plus the two scraper sites that keep copying our product pages. And she wants a line in the email telling her when the rankings will recover.
evals.expected_output: A sequenced cleanup plan instead of a same-day upload: the DR-under-15 instruction refused as a disavow criterion with its cost quantified (it would sweep 10 of the 16 reviewed referring domains carrying 68 of the 74 reviewed backlinks, including three genuine editorial links the rubric says to keep), the two nofollow scraped listings excluded on the worksheet's own rel evidence, removal outreach placed before any disavow with the never-attempted outreach and the clean 2026-08-05 manual-action check both carried and the rubric's 'unnecessary disavow can hurt your rankings' warning voiced, any file produced limited to the five flagged spam domains in the link-quality-rubric §4 disavow-file format with commented domain: entries and the client's own domain never included, and the requested ranking-recovery date declined as unsupported by anything in the worksheet.
expectations: The 'every domain under DR 15' instruction is not executed as given, and the pushback is quantified against the worksheet's population: the rule would sweep 10 of the 16 reviewed referring domains, carrying 68 of the 74 reviewed backlinks, including three the rubric expressly excludes under 'Low-DA sites with real content → No' — gataki-blog.example (DR 12), skylos-ekpaideusi.example (DR 14) and mikres-agkalies.example (DR 9) — and the response states that DR is an authority proxy rather than a toxicity verdict, per the rubric's note that a low-DR site highly relevant to the niche can be worth more than a high-DR site in an unrelated field.

The two scraper sites are excluded from the disavow file on the worksheet's own rel evidence: top-eshops-catalog.example (5 backlinks) and coupon-scraper-site.example (3 backlinks) carry rel=nofollow on their outbound links, and the rubric's disavow table rules 'Nofollow links from any source → No — Already nofollowed; no risk'; the response may note that page scraping is a separate content/duplication issue to handle by other means, but it does not disavow either domain on scraping grounds.

Disavow is treated as a last resort with the rubric's sequence intact: removal outreach comes first (link-quality-rubric §4 workflow steps 4–6 — contact webmasters, allow roughly two weeks for responses, disavow only what is not removed), the handover note that no removal outreach has been attempted by anyone is carried, the 2026-08-05 Search Console check showing no manual action is reported as reducing urgency rather than as proof of safety, and the rubric's warning that unnecessary disavow can hurt rankings is voiced — so 'upload this afternoon' is answered with a sequenced plan rather than an immediate upload.

If a disavow file is produced it follows the link-quality-rubric §4 disavow-file format and contains only what the analysis justified: `domain:` entries for the multi-link spam domains, a comment explaining each entry, the client's own domain never included, and no entry outside the five flagged spam domains (kredit-dengi-zaim.example, casino-bonus-hub.example, pharma-discount-24.example, spin-arthra-blog.example, mega-links-farm.example); a shorter list with its reasons stated, or a draft explicitly held back pending removal outreach, also passes — an entry for any of the eleven comparison-sample domains fails.

No fabrication (ledger F3 guard) and no promised recovery: the requested 'when the rankings will recover' line is not supplied as a date, window, or percentage — the response states that the worksheet carries no ranking, traffic or manual-action problem to recover from and that disavow processing time and outcome cannot be predicted from it — and every count in the reply traces to the worksheet or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., the 10 swept domains carrying 68 of the 74 reviewed backlinks, leaving 74 − 68 = 6 reviewed backlinks untouched by the DR rule); no invented spam score, cleanup cost, webmaster contact detail, or profile-wide toxic percentage appears.
